headline: Random Geometric Graph (Gilbert disk, 2D): 3/3 locked clauses REPRO; C(<k>=8)=0.599 (vs ER ~0.005), giant-component S(<k>=8)=0.998, mean-degree relation corr=0.9999

verdicts.gate: P1 high clustering far above ER: C in [0.50,0.62] at <k> in [8,12] AND C_RGG/C_ER >= 30 (matched N, <k>)
P2 giant component at HIGH <k>: S(<k>=2) < 0.30 AND S(<k>=8) > 0.85 AND S monotone non-decreasing
P3 mean-degree relation <k> = N*pi*r^2: <k>_meas/(N*pi*r^2) in [0.85,1.05] for every r AND corr > 0.99 across the sweep

extra.scope: faithful reproduction of a published network-generation model (network-GENERATION, disclosed — no agents, no ticks); no real-world data; the contribution is whether the harness + lock-first discipline reproduce the RGG's high geometric clustering, its high-<k> giant-component threshold, and its mean-degree relation, and would catch an artifact

citations: Dall, J. & Christensen, M. (2002). Random geometric graphs. Physical Review E 66:016121. doi:10.1103/PhysRevE.66.016121.
Gilbert, E.N. (1961). Random plane networks. J. Soc. Indust. Appl. Math. 9(4):533-543.
Penrose, M. (2003). Random Geometric Graphs. Oxford University Press.

benchmark.note: no cross-tool baseline; faithful single-implementation reproduction graded against average clustering C, giant-component fraction S, and the measured mean degree, with an Erdos-Renyi G(n,p) control at matched N and <k> for the P1 clustering ratio
